name: polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome overview
title: PMOS pathway: oligomenorrhoea or hyperandrogenism; exclude the seven mimics, read the total testosterone, and treat the symptom that distresses her, with the diagnostic triad (all three needed) across the top

any_of.heading: PMOS is diagnosed when ALL THREE are met:

items.title: Hyperandrogenism
lines: ~clinical exam OR labs (↑ testosterone)

items.title: Ovulatory dysfunction
lines: ~oligomenorrhoea OR cystic ovaries on ultrasound

items.title: Other disorders excluded
lines: ~the 7 mimics below

nodes.title: Oligomenorrhoea and/or hyperandrogenism
lines: ~renamed from polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in 2026: the follicles are arrested antral follicles, not cysts

nodes.title: History, exam + first-line labs
lines: beta-hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin) · prolactin · TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) · total testosterone
~pelvic ultrasound is NOT required

nodes.title: A mimic?
lines: ~the lecture's 7: exclude them first

nodes.title: NOT PMOS: mimics of oligomenorrhoea
lines: pregnancy: ↑ beta-hCG
hyperprolactinaemia: GALACTORRHOEA, ↑ prolactin (normal < 20 nmol/L)
hyperthyroidism: ↓ TSH, ↑ free T4
early menarche or menopause: menstrual history

nodes.title: NOT PMOS: mimics of hyperandrogenism
lines: exogenous testosterone, incl. a PARTNER's topical gel: medication + social history
tumour, ovary or adrenal: RAPID onset, ↑↑↑ testosterone → imaging
non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH): ↑ 17-hydroxyprogesterone

nodes.title: Read the total testosterone
lines: ~the only androgen used (not DHEAS or androstenedione) · female normal < 2 nmol/L

nodes.title: Normal (< 2 nmol/L)
lines: does NOT exclude PMOS: the exam (terminal male-pattern hair, acne, alopecia) can meet this limb

nodes.title: ~2.1–2.5 nmol/L
lines: slightly raised: fits PMOS

nodes.title: ~10 nmol/L: the male range
lines: NOT PMOS: think TUMOUR → imaging

nodes.title: PMOS: treat what distresses her
lines: ~and watch metabolic + endometrial risk in everyone

nodes.title: Hirsutism + hair
lines: surface: epilation, shaving, sugaring, waxing, laser
oral: antiandrogens (spironolactone, cyproterone) · birth control pill
topical: EFLORNITHINE
alopecia: MINOXIDIL 5%, antiandrogens, pill, transplant
~hirsutism is defined by her DISTRESS, not a score

nodes.title: Irregular cycles + endometrium
lines: birth control pill or cyclical progesterone · weight loss, exercise
WITHDRAWAL BLEEDS ≥ 4× a year: endometrial cancer is more common
ultrasound surveillance for endometrial hypertrophy

nodes.title: Subfertility
lines: lifestyle · induce ovulation with AROMATASE INHIBITORS
metformin (arguably) for early miscarriage
ovarian stroma surgery: RARE now

nodes.title: Metabolic risk
lines: hemoglobin A1c + lipid panel · monitor diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease
lifestyle: high fibre, low fat · 150 min vigorous exercise a week · MODEST weight loss
consider BARIATRIC surgery

nodes.title: NOT topical testosterone
lines: the one wrong treatment

nodes.title: She CAN conceive spontaneously
lines: → effective contraception if pregnancy is not wanted

nodes.title: NO body shaming
lines: NOT all with PMOS are overweight · a GENTLE weight history

panels.title: History + exam clues
items: menstrual history: how often at first, in the later teens, after 20
just stopped the pill, now irregular? the pill MASKED it
TERMINAL male-pattern hair: sides of face, chin, chest, upper arms
Ferriman-Gallwey score: 9 sites graded 1–4; ignores ethnicity + hair removal
acanthosis nigricans · skin tags · central adiposity (waist ÷ hip > 0.85)
PMOS is GRADUAL and has NO galactorrhoea

panels.title: Myths to dispel
items: TRUE: subfertility + early miscarriage · type 2 diabetes, hypertension, high lipids · endometrial cancer · mood disorders
FALSE: cannot lose weight · always hungry · an organic or vegan diet helps · cannot conceive
more common: gestational diabetes · frontal alopecia · NOT adrenal hypertrophy
no gold-standard test · insulin resistance is ASSOCIATED, not a 4th criterion
over 170 million women, up to 20% of reproductive age
